# Subscribe to premium in the app

## Problem Statement

Existing free users who use the habit tracker on two or more devices lose their streaks, because the free app keeps habits on one phone only; in the last quarter 1,200 support requests asked for sync between devices. The vision offers sync as part of a paid premium plan, but today such a user has no way to get premium from inside the app. This feature lets a free user see the premium offer at the monthly price the owner has set and subscribe without contacting support. The price itself is a business decision for the owner (Product Loop); this plan does not choose it and treats it as a value the owner sets.

## Business Alignment

**Job to Be Done:** When I use the habit tracker on two or more devices and my streaks stay behind on one phone, I want to subscribe to premium from inside the app, so I can keep the same habits and streaks on every device without contacting support.

**Impact Map:**
- **Goal:** Free users on two or more devices get sync between devices by subscribing to premium in the app, instead of filing support requests for it (1,200 in the last quarter, per the parent vision).
- **Actor:** An existing free user of the habit tracker who uses it on two or more devices (the vision's target audience).
- **Impact:** The user subscribes to premium inside the app on their own, with no contact with support.
- **Deliverable:** The in-app subscribe flow: the premium offer at the owner-set monthly price, payment, and premium status on the user's account, recognised on every device they sign in on.

**Alignment checks:**
1. Goal traces to the vision's problem statement (lost streaks on a second device; 1,200 sync requests): YES.
2. Actor is the vision's target audience: YES.
3. Impact is observable (a free user becomes premium inside the app, with no support contact; vision success criterion 1): YES.
4. Deliverable is one functional area (subscribing; the syncing of habits itself is not in this plan): YES.

## User Stories

**Story 1.** **As a** free user who uses the habit tracker on two or more devices, **I want** to subscribe to premium from inside the app at the monthly price it shows me, **so that** I get my habits and streaks on all my devices without contacting support.

**Story 2.** **As a** premium user, **I want** my premium plan to be recognised on every device I sign in on with my account, **so that** I keep premium on my tablet or new phone without paying a second time.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Scenario 1.1: Free user sees the premium offer at the owner-set price**
  Given a free user is signed in on their phone
  And the owner has set the monthly premium price
  When the user opens the premium offer from inside the app
  Then the offer states that premium keeps their habits and streaks on every device they sign in on
  And the offer shows the monthly price exactly as the owner set it, with its currency
  And no payment has been asked for yet

- [ ] **Scenario 1.2: Free user subscribes without contacting support**
  Given a signed-in free user is viewing the premium offer
  When they confirm the subscription and the payment goes through
  Then within 10 seconds of the payment going through, the app shows them as a premium user
  And the amount shown in the payment step equals the monthly price shown on the offer
  And every step from the offer to premium took place inside the app, with no step asking them to contact support

- [ ] **Scenario 1.3: Payment is declined or cancelled**
  Given a signed-in free user has confirmed the subscription
  When the payment is declined, or the user cancels the payment step
  Then the app shows a message that the subscription did not go through and that they have not been charged
  And the user is still on the free plan
  And every habit and streak on the device is shown unchanged
  And the user can open the premium offer again and subscribe

- [ ] **Scenario 1.4: Free user who is not signed in**
  Given a free user is not signed in to an account
  When they choose to subscribe from the premium offer
  Then the app asks them to sign in or create an account before any payment step is shown
  And after they sign in, they are back on the premium offer with the same monthly price
  And every habit and streak that was on the device before signing in is shown unchanged

- [ ] **Scenario 1.5: No price has been set by the owner**
  Given the owner has not set a monthly premium price
  When a free user opens the app
  Then no premium offer and no subscribe option is shown
  And no premium price is shown anywhere in the app

- [ ] **Scenario 2.1: Premium follows the account to another device**
  Given a user subscribed to premium on their phone
  When they sign in with the same account on their tablet
  Then within 10 seconds of signing in, the tablet shows them as a premium user
  And the tablet does not ask them to pay

- [ ] **Scenario 2.2: Premium user is not offered a second subscription**
  Given a premium user is signed in
  When they open the premium offer on any device signed in with their account
  Then the app shows that they already have premium
  And no option to buy premium again is shown

- [ ] **Scenario 2.3: Premium belongs to the account, not the device**
  Given a user subscribed to premium with account A on a tablet
  When a different account B signs in on that same tablet
  Then the tablet shows account B on the free plan
  And the tablet shows account B the premium offer

## Scope

### In Scope
- The premium offer inside the app, naming what premium gives (the same habits and streaks on every device the user signs in on) and the owner-set monthly price with its currency; no offer and no price while the owner has not set one (Scenarios 1.1, 1.5).
- Subscribing to premium from inside the app, charged the monthly price shown on the offer, with no support contact (Scenario 1.2).
- A declined or cancelled payment: the user is told it did not go through, stays on the free plan, keeps every habit and streak, and can try again (Scenario 1.3).
- Sign-in or account creation before payment, with the habits already on the device kept (Scenario 1.4). Documented choice: premium attaches to the user's account, because the vision's success criterion is "A premium user sees the same habits and streaks on every device they sign in on"; a purchase tied to one device could not follow the user to a second one.
- Premium recognised on every device signed in with the subscribing account, no second purchase offered, and premium not shared with other accounts on the same device (Scenarios 2.1, 2.2, 2.3).

### Out of Scope
- Choosing the monthly premium price and its currency: a business decision for the owner, made in the Product Loop (docs/PRODUCT_LOOP.md) outside this technical pipeline. It was surfaced to the owner in this plan's status file on 2026-10-06 and is still open; this plan treats the price as a value the owner sets.
- Syncing habits and streaks between devices for premium users: in the parent vision's scope, but no functional stub for it exists (Glob `plans/functional/habit-tracker-premium-*.md` matched 1 file, this one; Grep `sync` in `plans/` matched only the vision, lines 13, 14 and 27). Whether and when a stub for it is added is the owner's decision.
- Team or family plans: excluded by the parent vision.
- The web version of the app: excluded by the parent vision.
- Free trials, an annual plan, or more than one premium tier: business-model decisions for the owner (Product Loop); not in the vision or any stub of it.
- Cancelling, pausing or changing a subscription, and refunds: not in the vision's success criteria and not in any stub of it; whether and when a stub for them is added is the owner's decision.
- Which payment provider or app-store billing is used, and how premium status is stored: how it is built, which belongs in the implementation plan.

## Risks

### Technical Risks
- App-store billing rules: selling a digital subscription inside a phone or tablet app can be bound by the app stores' own billing rules, which decide how payment is taken and how the subscription is recognised on other devices.
  - Likelihood: HIGH
  - Impact: MEDIUM
  - Mitigation: Confirm in the implementation plan which store billing rules apply on each platform the app ships on, before the payment step is designed.
- No sign-in in the free app today: the vision says the free app keeps habits on one phone only, and neither the vision nor the stub says whether the app has accounts. If it has none, Scenario 1.4 needs an account sign-in that does not exist yet.
  - Likelihood: MEDIUM
  - Impact: HIGH
  - Mitigation: Review the current app for an existing sign-in before the implementation plan is written; if there is none, list account sign-in in the implementation plan as a dependency for the owner to schedule.
- Delayed payment confirmation: confirmation that a payment went through can arrive late, so the 10-second thresholds in Scenarios 1.2 and 2.1 may fail.
  - Likelihood: MEDIUM
  - Impact: MEDIUM
  - Mitigation: Test the time from payment to premium shown against the payment provider's test environment during the build, and bring the measured time to the owner if 10 seconds cannot be met.

### Business Risks
- Price not set: the monthly price is still the owner's open decision, and by Scenario 1.5 no subscribe option reaches users until it is set.
  - Likelihood: HIGH
  - Impact: MEDIUM
  - Mitigation: Obtain the monthly price and its currency from the owner through the Product Loop; the plan already treats the price as an owner-set value, so setting it needs no change to this plan.

### Dependency Risks
- Paying for sync that has no plan: premium's value to the user is sync between devices, and no functional stub for sync exists. If subscribing reaches users before sync works, users pay for something they do not get.
  - Likelihood: MEDIUM
  - Impact: HIGH
  - Mitigation: Ask the owner whether a functional stub for syncing habits for premium users should be added to this vision; the order in which the two are built is the owner's decision.

## Priority

**Priority: HIGH** (Score: 8/9)
- Dependency: 2 -- no stub in `plans/functional/` depends on this one and this one depends on none (`depends_on: "none"`); the vision's sync for premium users would need premium status, but no sync stub exists.
- Business Impact: 3 -- core to the vision's primary goal; it is the vision's first success criterion ("A free user can subscribe to premium from inside the app without contacting support").
- Technical Risk: 3 -- a payment integration with outside billing, plus premium status that must follow the account across devices.
